brief: A compact desk unit with a drawer, plus a spike at a corner where three bases meet to hold a small platform.

requirements.evidence: It is only three bases (piece:0,0,0, piece:1,0,0 and piece:1,-1,0 half-s) on one level, with top covers. The open side faces have end caps (capOpenFaces) and the joints are bolted (lockJoints).
drawer:0#1,-1#cut sits on the north cut face of the half base at (1,-1).

requirements.requirement: A spike at a corner where three bases meet
requirements.evidence: spike:0#0,0|1,-1|1,0 stands where cells (0,0), (1,-1) and (1,0) meet. It is the mount type, because a solid spike can't carry a platform. My first layout put the drawer in this corner and the spike was refused (SPIKE_CLASH), so I changed the half base to face the other way.
The small platform (platform-sm) is fitted on the mount spike.

finish.summary: I built a compact desk unit from three bases at level 0: full bases at (0,0) and (1,0), and a south-half base at (1,-1). A drawer sits on the cut face of the half base, and a mount spike with a small platform stands at the corner where the three bases meet. The bases have top covers, the open side faces have end caps and the joints are bolted. The final check found no rule errors and no mesh collisions ("clear"). In total it has 28 parts, needs about 1.4 kg of filament and takes about 2,024 minutes (roughly 34 hours) to print. I didn't add any props because the brief didn't ask for them.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
